subject.title: fix: use atomic writes for crash-safety on exec approvals, restart sentinel, shell profile, and saveJsonFile

question: Should the remaining shell completion profile writes be fixed now with a narrow maintainer-owned patch, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept the residual crash-safety risk?
rationale: The source-level bug is still present, but the change rewrites user shell startup files and the issue already carries no-new-fix-pr and maintainer-review routing labels, so automation should not queue a fix without maintainer intent.

options.title: Maintainer-owned narrow fix
options.body: A maintainer owns or explicitly approves a focused patch that routes profile creation and update through the atomic text writer while preserving current profile selection and permissions.

options.title: Allow ClawSweeper repair
options.body: A maintainer removes the no-new-fix-pr intent and lets ClawSweeper attempt the same narrow atomic-write patch with focused completion tests.

options.title: Accept residual risk
options.body: Maintainers document that shell-profile writes remain best-effort and close or downgrade this cleanup despite the source-level crash-safety gap.

recommendation.title: Maintainer-owned narrow fix
recommendation.body: A maintainer owns or explicitly approves a focused patch that routes profile creation and update through the atomic text writer while preserving current profile selection and permissions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent completion-runtime and related persistence work makes this the best available routing candidate for the remaining shell-profile decision.
